Machinery Manufacturer Kiran Engineering to Set Up New Plant in Gujarat

AHMEDABAD, India, June 13 — Kiran Engineering, a leading player in India's machinery sector, announced Thursday plans to invest INR 650 crore ($78 million) in a new manufacturing facility in Gujarat, aiming to boost its production capacity and meet rising domestic and export demand.

The new plant, to be located in the Sanand industrial corridor near Ahmedabad, will focus on producing precision equipment for the automotive, agriculture, and construction sectors. Construction is scheduled to begin in August, with operations expected to commence by mid-2026, the company said in a statement.

"We are witnessing strong growth in demand for advanced machinery solutions, both within India and in overseas markets," said Anil Deshmukh, Managing Director of Kiran Engineering. "This investment underlines our commitment to supporting the Make in India initiative as well as the growing needs of our clients."

Deshmukh added that the facility is projected to create around 1,200 direct jobs and hundreds more indirectly through supply chains. The expansion will increase the company's annual output by 35 percent, according to company estimates.

Industry analysts say the move reflects optimism in the sector, which has benefited from robust infrastructure spending and expanding manufacturing activity. "India's machinery industry has seen double-digit growth rates over the past three years," said Nisha Rathi, an analyst at Mumbai-based NeoMarkets Research. "Kiran Engineering's decision to expand in Gujarat is in line with the state’s emergence as a manufacturing hub, supported by strong logistics and an investor-friendly environment."

The Gujarat government welcomed the announcement, noting that it fits with the state’s drive to attract high-value manufacturing investments. "We are pleased that Kiran Engineering has chosen Gujarat for their expansion," said state Industries Minister R. V. Patel. "This will further strengthen our industrial base and generate quality employment opportunities for local talent."

The Indian Machinery Manufacturers’ Association also lauded the development, saying it would bolster the industry’s export potential. According to the association, machinery exports from India rose 18 percent last year to $5.7 billion, driven by demand from Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Africa.
